risks.risk: Item mismatch: seller may be offering sand, but photos show IBC tanks (or vice versa).
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the actual item being sold (sand bag/pile with label, or the IBC tank with visible markings) and the exact quantity/unit.
risks.if_unproven: Price as the worst-case interpretation from the photo (used IBC tank) and treat any sand/material claims as not included.

risks.risk: IBC tank condition/cleanliness: could be contaminated from previous contents (chemical residue, odor, staining).
risks.proof: Request photos of the inside (open top if possible) and the outlet/valve area, plus a statement of last contents with any label/trace.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed clean/food-grade (assume only general-purpose storage).

risks.risk: Capacity/size uncertainty (e.g., 1000L vs other sizes) affects price.
risks.proof: Request a photo of the capacity marking on the IBC (usually on the label/sticker) or a tape-measure/known model label.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest likely capacity/most common used size only if confirmed; otherwise treat as generic used IBC with no capacity premium.

risks.risk: Leak/damage risk (cracks, cage damage, valve failure) not visible in one angle.
risks.proof: Request a short video showing the valve/outlet, checking for cracks, and (if possible) a pressure/leak test statement.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially needing inspection/repair (no working guarantee).

proof_requests: Confirm what is actually for sale: sand or IBC tanks (send 2–3 clear photos of the exact item).
If IBC tanks: send photos of the label showing capacity and any previous contents/chemical compatibility.
Send close-ups of the valve/outlet and any visible damage; ideally a short video of the tank condition.
response.reason: The photo shows IBC tanks, while the seller’s text talks about “white sand” and chemical/health claims; without clear identity and condition details, a reliable price cannot be set.
